analysis: All changes are docs. docs/developer/test.md only updates its date and references tests (e.g. scripts/test-release-dev-branch.py pinning the dev-branch lane: dispatch-only, no tag, no prod environment, no signing identity, DEV_RELEASE_KEY only). No security-relevant change there. docs/operations/provider-release.md (head ~337-380) documents a new experimental dev-branch lane (.github/workflows/release-dev-branch.yml) and an installer change (scripts/install.sh, select_provider_identity/verify_staged_app_signature) that accepts ad-hoc signed builds. For versions containing -dev./-staging., the designated requirement is relaxed to the bundle ID only, dropping the Apple anchor and team OU. The dev coordinator hashes the bundle and does not inspect the Apple signature. Open points for the next pass: the actual workflow and installer source were not supplied, so enforcement of 'no secret in the build job' and 'prod coordinator never served a pre-release' is unverified. Shared bundle ID, APNs topic and fan helper (TB-010/T-044) interact with self-signed builds. Relationship to T-054/A-017 durable build qualification and require_app_attest_qualification=true for ad-hoc builds is unclear. Branch builds become dev latest by created_at.

findings.detail: The new docs describe `select_provider_identity` and `verify_staged_app_signature` relaxing the designated requirement to only the bundle identifier `io.darkbloom.provider` whenever the version string contains `-dev.` or `-staging.`. The only code-identity check left is the identifier, so any ad-hoc binary with that identifier passes. The selector is a substring of the version returned by the release API. The safety argument relies on 'a prod coordinator is never served a pre-release version', which is an unverified deployment assumption. A mis-registered, compromised or poisoned release response carrying a `-dev.` marker would downgrade the installer to unsigned-code acceptance on a production machine. The dev and prod installs also share the bundle identifier, APNs topic and the root fan helper `io.darkbloom.fan-helper`. This weakens the code-identity assumptions behind T-013, T-034, T-054 and T-044, and the threat model does not describe the new self-signed tier. Fix: gate the relaxed requirement on the installer's dev coordinator binding (the host it was fetched from), not on the returned version string. Refuse the marker when the prod coordinator is bound. Confirm the fan helper and MDM/APNs paths still require the Developer ID team requirement. Add the self-signed tier to TB-009, TB-011 and T-054.
findings.title: Installer drops Apple-anchor/team check for any `-dev.`/`-staging.` version, accepting arbitrary ad-hoc code

findings.detail: The new `release-dev-branch.yml` lane lets any workflow-dispatch writer publish a build of any `ref` to the dev coordinator with `DEV_RELEASE_KEY`, without merge or review. The docs state that, because `/v1/releases/latest` orders by `created_at`, the branch build becomes the latest dev release and a fresh install takes it. The dev coordinator 'hashes the bundle rather than inspecting the Apple signature', so registration of a self-signed build does not imply the Developer ID identity assumed in T-054 and A-017. Provider operators on dev could be served unreviewed code that handles consumer plaintext (A-001). Mitigations to document or enforce: restrict dispatchers, require a protected environment or approval for `DEV_RELEASE_KEY`, avoid `latest` aliasing for branch builds (use an opt-in channel), and record in the threat model that dev-tier providers must never receive production-sensitive traffic.
findings.title: Dispatch of arbitrary branch publishes unreviewed code as dev `latest` for fresh installs
